root.name: Queen's Indian Defense: Riumin Variation
root.moves: 1. d4 Nf6 2. c4 e6 3. Nf3 b6 4. g3 Bb7 5. Bg2 Bb4+ 6. Bd2 Be7

overview: White fianchettoes against the Queen's Indian and Black pins the knight with ...Bb4+, then retreats to e7 after Bd2, so Black has gained little but White has the bishop on d2. After 7.Nc3 O-O 8.O-O Black usually plays ...d5 or ...Ne4. Both sides develop slowly and the game is positional.

white_ideas.idea: Fianchetto on g2 and castle, then push d5 or e4
Use the bishop pair and the long diagonal

black_ideas.idea: Fianchetto on b7, hold e4 and play ...d5 or ...Ne4
Trade pieces and keep a sound centre

character.notes: Slow manoeuvring with few forcing lines.

soundness.notes: The line is a respected, safe set-up for both sides.

structure.notes: The centre is tense with c4/d4 against ...e6/...d5 or ...Ne4 and can be resolved either way.

approach.notes: Played by strong players against 1.d4 as a normal Indian line.

level.notes: Plans are positional and the theory is moderate.

character.reason: Black's set-up is hard to break and play is steady.

soundness.reason: Both sides play a mainstream line.

structure.reason: Black keeps the centre in tension with ...d5 or ...Ne4 and White keeps c4/d4.

approach.reason: It is a normal Queen's Indian branch, not a set-up played against everything.

level.reason: The plans are positional and need understanding.

plans.reason: Both sides put bishops on the long diagonals.
